name: Jumilla
terms: Denominación de Origen Calificada, a step above DO for regions with a record of consistent quality. Only Rioja and Priorat hold it.
Denominación de Origen, Spain's main quality tier.
Spain's regional wine tier, below DO.
A single-estate wine of high quality. A pago is a vineyard estate.
Young wine, sold with little or no aging. Some see a few months in oak.

notes: Monastrell is Jumilla's key grape, tough enough for drought, summer heat and spring frost.
It gives broad, fleshy wines with good alcohol and acidity, ripe fruit and well-integrated tannin.
The reds run from violet to brick red, with red and black fruit, and are tannic.
Other grapes add color stability, acidity and aging potential.
Sweet and fortified Monastrell wines add dried fruit notes.

blurb.text: A DO across northern Murcia and southeastern Albacete. Allowed grapes include Monastrell, Tempranillo, Syrah, Garnacha Tinta and Cabernet Sauvignon.
